title: Tighten st3_settings_switch_a11y_test.dart to assert the Hebrew-Terms Switch specifically, not any labelled Switch
rule: TQ-8 (assertion weaker than what the source can do wrong)
why: S1's assertion loops every `Switch` widget found in SettingsScreen and passes as soon as ANY of them has a non-empty semantics label — it never isolates the Hebrew-Terms tile's own Switch. Today settings_screen.dart has exactly one bare `Switch(` (confirmed by grep), so the test is currently equivalent to the intended check, but that equivalence is accidental, not encoded. A second labelled Switch added anywhere else on the (816-line, HOTSPOT) SettingsScreen in a future change would make this ST-3 regression guard keep passing even if `_HebrewTermsTile`'s own `Semantics(label: ...)` wrapper were removed or broken.
recommendation: Locate the Switch that is a descendant of the PreferenceListTile carrying l10n.hebrewTermsPreference (or add a Key to _HebrewTermsTile's Switch) and assert that specific Switch's semantics label contains/equals l10n.hebrewTermsPreference, not 'any switch in the screen has a label'.
acceptance_criteria: The test fails if a second, unrelated, labelled Switch is added to SettingsScreen while _HebrewTermsTile's Semantics wrapper is removed.

corrections: Cited line 135 should be 136; the quoted 'if (semanticsNode.label.isNotEmpty) {' / 'foundLabelledSwitch = true;' pair is actually lines 136-137 per grep -n.
Evidence item 1 cites line 135; the quoted text ('if (semanticsNode.label.isNotEmpty) {') actually begins at line 136. Quote text itself is accurate and easily located.
